title: Operate Ansible through Semaphore
objective: Connect repositories, inventories, credentials, environments, and task templates in a controlled automation service.

sourceAlignment.title: Complete Ansible Semaphore Tutorial: From Installation to Automation
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Semaphore provides a web interface and API around Ansible execution. Installation is only the first layer; useful automation requires a database, an application configuration, and a service process with protected access.
A project connects the execution ingredients: a version-controlled repository, inventory, key store, environment variables, and a task template that selects the playbook and launch options.

Central execution improves repeatability and visibility but also concentrates credentials and authority. Apply authentication, least privilege, TLS, backups, and audit-log retention before treating the service as production infrastructure.
explanation.rule: A controller UI governs Ansible execution; it does not replace reviewed repositories or least privilege.

examples.title: Working design or automation artifact
examples.code:
semaphore_project:
  repository: git
  inventory: managed
  credentials: key_store
  environment: protected
  execution: task_template
  audit_logs: retained
examples.note: Read the structure, predict its effect, then adapt it in the assignment and terminal mission.

checks.question: Which practice best supports this lesson’s objective: “Connect repositories, inventories, credentials, environments, and task templates in a controlled automation service.”?
options: Preview scope, use state-aware modules, and verify the observed result.
Hide failures and assume the target state was reached.
Store credentials beside the playbook in plaintext.
Replace every module with an unreviewed shell command.

feedback.correct: Correct—safe automation combines explicit scope, desired state, and verification.
feedback.incorrect: The reliable workflow makes scope, state, and verification visible.

lab.title: Audit a controller design
lab.setup: Start the disposable lab with npm run lab:up, then work from /workspace in the Terminal tab.
steps: List where repository, inventory, and credential data originate.
Identify which users may launch production templates.
Record backup and TLS requirements before installation.

lab.success: The design separates source, targets, secrets, authorization, and audit history.
